## Season so far

Kenneth Walker III has been the clear lead back in Kansas City's offense. Through 8 games he has 183.4 half-PPR points (22.9 per game), 159 carries for 872 yards and 7 TDs, plus 26 catches for 172 yards and 4 more TDs. His season is built on spikes: 32.6 in Week 1, 30.4 in Week 4, 26.9 in Week 6 and 34.3 in Week 9. In between were three flat games of 20.8, 20.3 and 10.4, and a 7.7 dud in Week 7 (14 carries for 36 yards). Week 9 against the Jets (18 carries for 102 yards, plus four catches on four targets for 41 yards and two TDs) was the best result of the year. The role itself hasn't changed. He plays about 74% of snaps and takes 42% of the team's carries and targets, second among RBs.

## Usage and efficiency

The volume is real. He has 34 red-zone carries and 15 goal-line carries on the season, and 9 red-zone targets. The last 4 games look a little lighter than the full season:

| | Season | Last 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Points per game | 22.9 | 19.8 |
| Yards per carry | 5.5 | 4.7 |
| Target share | 15% | 13% |
| Opportunity share | 42% | 39% |
| Snaps | 74% | 74% |

Snaps are unchanged. Opportunity share dipped by three points, and the dip is mostly Emmett Johnson picking up targets (11 of them in that stretch).

The touchdowns look earned. He has 11 TDs against 10.8 expected from where his carries and targets came, so that part isn't luck. The yards per carry is the part that is likely to come down. His 5.5 is second among 37 RBs, against 4.2 for RBs overall, and the last 4 games already show it settling at 4.7. Receiving is modest at 4.8 yards per target, so his value there comes from TDs, not yardage. Kansas City runs only 58 plays a game (18th most), which caps the volume.

## Health and situation

I found no verified injury for Walker this week. A foot issue showed up in August and didn't linger. Rotowire and the Fantasy Footballers had nothing current. Check Wednesday and Thursday practice reports before kickoff, since I couldn't confirm a Week 10 report.

The backfield is thin behind him. Johnson is the clear No. 2 with 10 carries, 11 targets and 26% of snaps over the last 4 games, a 9% season share. Brashard Smith is on IR with a hamstring, which is why he hasn't been a factor. Hamstring injuries tend to linger and re-aggravate, and I'd expect him back no sooner than mid-season. Ben VanSumeren is out for a coach's decision. If Walker were to miss time, Johnson would be the main beneficiary. Also, one note called Johnson "overshadowing" a rookie backup in the Week 8 loss, so watch whether his receiving role keeps growing.

## Outlook

The remaining schedule is Week 10 at ATL (easy), Week 11 vs ARI (neutral), Week 12 at BUF (easy) and Week 13 at LAR (tough). After that, 9 games remain and the bye is in Week 5. The projection is 192.6 points over those games, or 21.3 per game. Fair value is about 21.5, below his actual 22.9. That gap is the efficiency, which I expect to regress a bit.

Floor is real: he had 7.7 and 10.4 point games when the touchdowns didn't come. The ceiling is 30 or more, which he has hit four times.

**Treat him as a must-start every week, with no sitting him for matchups.** Holders should hold. If a manager will pay full price for the 22.9 points per game, selling is reasonable, but only for a true top-tier return. Don't sell for depth.
